summary.text: 白 is used for “white.” Its early graph is interpreted as a picture, but its referent is disputed: proposals include a thumb and a cooking or measuring vessel.

formation.text: Pictographic: the early graph is treated as one picture, though its subject is unsettled. One interpretation identifies a thumb; another proposes a cooking or measuring vessel, with the middle stroke marking the join between lid and body. Neither is established as consensus.

components.text: The early graph is treated as one pictorial form, not as separate components. Competing interpretations identify it as a thumb or a vessel; its original referent remains unresolved.

history.text: The curated script-style forms show an early rounded outline with two interior strokes, a bronze-style form with a pointed upper outline and two interior strokes, and a seal-style form with a taller central stroke and divided body. They illustrate graphic variation, not a proven sequence of dated inscriptions or a settled origin.
The Shuowen tradition explains the seal form as 入 joined with 二, interpreting 二 as an “yin number.” This is a historical explanation, not confirmation of the early pictorial origin.

uncertainties.text: Other proposed subjects include cloth, flame or light, and a face or head. The vessel proposal does not establish the ancient name or pronunciation of the object.

Early uses are reported for the color word 白, 伯, and a place name, but their order and first-attestation dates are unresolved. A thumb-based account explains 伯 through the thumb’s proposed leading position; a competing account proposes a sound-based borrowing, but does not establish the sound match. The reported use of 白 for “hundred” has no secure semantic link to “white.”
Comparative proposals for the spoken word 白 differ; neither identifies a sound-bearing component in the graph.

limitations.text: The order of early uses and exact first-attestation dates remain unresolved. The proposed sound-based borrowing involving 伯 does not establish a direction or prove that “white” developed from the depicted object, whose name and pronunciation are also unresolved.
The reported use for “hundred” does not establish a semantic transition from “white.”
The recorded glosses “pure, unblemished” and “bright” have no dated histories connecting them to earlier senses.

overview.text: 白 means “white.” Its early form was pictorial, but the subject is disputed; the familiar outline cannot settle whether it showed a thumb or a vessel.

components.text: Treat the early form as one picture: proposals identify a thumb or a vessel, but neither is settled.

takeaway.text: Accounts disagree about whether 白 was first used for 伯 or for “white.” One proposes reuse because the words sounded alike, but the ancient sound match is not established.
